dlg.q_slimes.offer.0: Something seeps out of the north well again. Same as every month, except this time it has opinions.
dlg.q_slimes.offer.1: Put down {count} {target} before they reach the market. And do not drink the water until you are done.
dlg.q_slimes.more.0: That well was fine for two hundred years. Then a Pulse. Now it gives water, slime, and once, a very confused eel.
dlg.q_slimes.more.1: Do not taste it to check. The last man who did said 'nothing', and that is exactly the problem.
dlg.q_slimes.wait.0: Still seeping. Still north. Still not for drinking.
dlg.q_slimes.done.0: The well smells like a well again. I will drink from it in a week. Or a year. Thank you.
dlg.q_slimes.done.1: Take your reward before I remember how much it costs.
dlg.q_wolves.offer.0: Wolves circle the wall every night. They never cross it. They know something we forgot.
dlg.q_wolves.offer.1: I would like to know what, but not enough to ask a wolf. Thin out {count} {target}, please.
dlg.q_wolves.more.0: They smell anchor stone and keep their distance. Clever. It is the only reason I have not gone out there to apologise.
dlg.q_wolves.more.1: Go by daylight. Wolves are polite in daylight. Mostly they are asleep.
dlg.q_wolves.wait.0: I can hear them from here. They sound well fed. That is not a compliment.
dlg.q_wolves.done.0: Quieter already. For once the wall can hear itself think.
dlg.q_wolves.done.1: Here is your reward. And a word of advice: never howl back.
dlg.q_scorpions.offer.0: Since the last Pulse, the sand out east moves wrong. So do the scorpions.
dlg.q_scorpions.offer.1: Their shells are harder than shells should be. {count} {target} ought to teach them manners.
dlg.q_scorpions.more.0: A Pulse changes one thing at a time. This one picked hardness. Last time it picked goats.
dlg.q_scorpions.more.1: Mind your boots. Sand that moves wrong tends to go for the boots first.
dlg.q_scorpions.wait.0: The sand is still moving. I stood at the wall and watched it for an hour. Do not do that.
dlg.q_scorpions.done.0: The east is quiet. Suspiciously quiet, but I will take suspicious over stung.
dlg.q_scorpions.done.1: Your reward, as promised. Keep the shell bits out of my hall.
dlg.q_swarm.offer.0: There is a tear by the old mill, and it keeps leaking. A little more every day.
dlg.q_swarm.offer.1: The miller says the flour is fine. The miller says that daily. The miller has not looked at the flour.
dlg.q_swarm.offer.2: Slow it down. {count} {target} should do it.
dlg.q_swarm.more.0: A tear is a small crack in the world. Things seep through. Slime is the polite option.
dlg.q_swarm.more.1: We cannot sew it shut. Nobody remembers how, or with what. So we hit whatever comes out.
dlg.q_swarm.wait.0: Still leaking. The miller says the mill is fine. The mill looks worse than the miller.
dlg.q_swarm.done.0: It still leaks, but slowly. Slow I can live with. I have lived with slow for sixty years.
dlg.q_swarm.done.1: Your reward. Spend it before a Pulse turns it into something else.
dlg.q_cull.offer.0: The wall holds as long as we pay for it. In stone, or in blood. Stone is scarce.
dlg.q_cull.offer.1: So: {count} of anything that walks, crawls, or looks at the wall funny. Call it a tithe.
dlg.q_cull.more.0: Every block cost something. A cart, a cousin, a harvest. Do not scratch it.
dlg.q_cull.more.1: I keep the ledger. The ledger has a column for blood. I am not proud of the column.
dlg.q_cull.wait.0: The column is still short. Count carefully. The wall does.
dlg.q_cull.done.0: Paid in full. The wall will remember this. It is the only one in town that remembers anything.
dlg.q_cull.done.1: Here is your reward. If anyone asks, the ledger says you did it for the town.
dlg.q_packleader.offer.0: One pack remembers the wall from before. Its leader teaches the others to go around it, and they have been going around a lot.
dlg.q_packleader.offer.1: Break the pack. Find the leader and finish it. I have a ring for whoever does.
dlg.q_packleader.more.0: Surveyors of the Ring wore that kind. I found it under the old gate. I was told not to polish it, so I polished it.
dlg.q_packleader.more.1: Yes, I said Ring. Capital R. Do not ask me what it was. I only own the receipt.
dlg.q_packleader.wait.0: The pack was at the wall again last night. Taking notes, I think.
dlg.q_packleader.done.0: Scattered. Without its leader it is just wolves again. Wolves I can manage.
dlg.q_packleader.done.1: Take the ring. It looks better on you than on my shelf. Odd. It almost seems to know you.
dlg.m1.offer.0: Take this: a shard of the stone our wall was cut from. Grey, warm, faintly rude.
dlg.m1.offer.1: {chronicler}, the chronicler in {town}, collects things that should not exist. Show it to them.
dlg.m1.offer.2: It is a walk. Take boots and a spare opinion.
dlg.m1.more.0: It sat on my shelf for thirty years. Last night it hummed. I do not like objects that hum without being asked.
dlg.m1.more.1: {chronicler} is odd, honest, and mostly right. A rare set. Do not accept the tea.
dlg.m1.wait.0: Still carrying it? Good. The shard wants {town}. Do not ask me how I know.
dlg.m1.done.0: Where did you get this? No, do not answer. Put it down. Gently. Gently!
dlg.m1.done.1: I will need three plates of the old world before I say more. I would also like a chair.
dlg.plate.crypt.offer.0: A calibration plate. Bolted to the control room wall, if the night-duty logs are right. Logs are rarely right.
dlg.plate.crypt.offer.1: It lies in the {dungeon}, under whatever keeps it now. Bring it up. Preferably with you still attached.
dlg.plate.crypt.more.0: The logs end mid-sentence. All of them. At some point that stops being a coincidence and becomes a pattern.
dlg.plate.crypt.more.1: People call it a crypt. My oldest papers call it a "bunker", whatever that was. People will call anything a crypt if enough of them died in it.
dlg.plate.crypt.wait.0: Still not back from the {dungeon}? The plate will not walk out on its own. I asked it.
dlg.plate.crypt.done.0: It is warm. Plates should not be warm after three hundred years. Hold on, I need to sit.
dlg.plate.crypt.done.1: Someone scratched a note under it. 'Too late.' People had such a sense of timing back then.
dlg.plate.ice.offer.0: The second plate was kept cold, they say, so that it would remember. Do not ask me how cold works that way.
dlg.plate.ice.offer.1: Look in the {dungeon}. Dress warmly. Dress as if you are being buried, but upright.
dlg.plate.ice.more.0: My papers call it a "cold-storage lab". I do not know what that is either. The guards there are very polite. That is the part that should worry you.
dlg.plate.ice.more.1: If anything asks for your badge, apologise. Old systems adore an apology.
dlg.plate.ice.wait.0: Cold, is it? Good. Cold keeps things. Including, I am told, plates.
dlg.plate.ice.done.0: The numbers in this frost change when I look away. I have stopped looking. Pass me a blanket.
dlg.plate.ice.done.1: Two down. I have never been so close to the truth, or so far from lunch.
dlg.plate.tomb.offer.0: The last plate is with the self-made king of the {dungeon}. He will not want to give it up.
dlg.plate.tomb.offer.1: Nobody ever asked him nicely. I suggest you try that first, and then do the other thing.
dlg.plate.tomb.more.0: He was senior on shift, so he declared himself king. Nobody objected. Nobody was left to.
dlg.plate.tomb.more.1: Bring me the plate. Leave the crown. It is improvised, and he is very sensitive about it.
dlg.plate.tomb.wait.0: The king receives no visitors. That has never stopped anyone, and perhaps it should have.
dlg.plate.tomb.done.0: A map. Rings of lines around one point, far beyond the last town on any map. Someone drew this by hand.
dlg.plate.tomb.done.1: Three plates. I know where they go next. I will tell you in a moment, after I stop shaking.
dlg.m5.offer.0: I have read what I can. The rest is in {capital}, in the ledgers that {ruler} keeps.
dlg.m5.offer.1: With the plates, those ledgers can finally be read. Take them there. Do not lose them. Do not read them in public.
dlg.m5.offer.2: Go before the next Pulse rewrites my nerve.
dlg.m5.more.0: Ledgers are guarded the way ledgers always are: by clerks. Be polite and carry a pen.
dlg.m5.more.1: The Crown keeps records and loses the explanations. The plates are the explanation.
dlg.m5.wait.0: {capital} is waiting. So is the next Pulse. I would not make them meet.
dlg.m5.offer.ended.0: I have read what I can. The rest is in {capital}, in the ledgers that {ruler} keeps.
dlg.m5.offer.ended.1: With the plates, those ledgers can finally be read. Take them there. Do not lose them. Do not read them in public.
dlg.m5.offer.ended.2: The ground has sounded different since you came back from the edge. Whatever you did there, the Crown will want it written down.
dlg.m5.wait.ended.0: {capital} is waiting. The ledgers have waited three hundred years. They are not getting more patient.
dlg.m5.done.0: Put them on the ledgers. Gently. By the ledger I have waited forty years for this. By the mirror, nine.
dlg.m5.done.1: The lines match. The Shift was no accident that broke the Ring. The Ring did it. It still runs, and now it is what holds all of us up.
dlg.m5.done.2: One more page. The Ring's "night shift": twelve faces, eleven crossed out. I have been looking at the twelfth since you walked in.
dlg.m5.done.ended.0: Put them on the ledgers. Gently. By the ledger I have waited forty years for this. By the mirror, nine.
dlg.m5.done.ended.1: The lines match. The Shift was no accident that broke the Ring. The Ring did it. And you have already been down there.
dlg.m5.done.ended.2: One more page. The Ring's "night shift": twelve faces, eleven crossed out. I have been looking at the twelfth since you walked in.
dlg.m6.offer.0: The ledger is clear. The Ring lies under the ground, about {far} tiles {dir} of {capital}, where nothing safe has stood for three hundred years.
dlg.m6.offer.1: Go down. Then decide for all of us. I could not.
dlg.m6.offer.2: Take supplies. Take courage, if you have a spare. Take a lantern, for certain.
dlg.m6.more.0: Fold it back and the Pulses stop. Leave it open and they never will. I argued both sides for a month, and lost both.
dlg.m6.more.1: My ledger and the plate agree on where it is. That has never happened before. I find it more frightening than the Ring.
dlg.m6.wait.0: Still here? The Ring is {far} tiles {dir}. It will not come to us. Lately I would not rule it out.
dlg.m6.reply.accept: Down to the Ring. Of course it is down.
dlg.m6.offer.ended.0: The ledger says the Ring lies {far} tiles {dir} of {capital}. From the look of your boots, you know that already.
dlg.m6.offer.ended.1: So it is done, one way or the other. I had a speech about deciding for all of us. I will save it for my grandchildren.
dlg.m6.offer.ended.2: All that is left is the telling. Sit. Tell me slowly, and do not spare me.
dlg.m6.more.ended.0: I argued both sides for a month and lost both. You did not have a month. Tell me which side won.
dlg.m6.wait.ended.0: You have been down there. I can see it on you. Tell me when you are ready.
dlg.m6.reply.accept.ended: I've been down. Let me tell you.
dlg.gen.bounty.0.offer.0: A prize goat went missing last week. The owner swears {target} took it, and he swore it at me, loudly.
dlg.gen.bounty.0.offer.1: Kill {count} {target} and he might stop shouting. I am not fussy about which ones.
dlg.gen.bounty.0.more.0: That goat won three ribbons and survived a Pulse. It could count to seven. Do not tell him it is probably fine.
dlg.gen.bounty.0.more.1: If you find a talking goat out there, it is him. Ask where he has been. Then ask him to stop.
dlg.gen.bounty.0.wait.0: The owner is back. I have run out of desks to hide under. Keep going.
dlg.gen.bounty.0.done.0: He cried. Then he sent me a cheese. Goat still missing. Village calmer. I call that a win.
dlg.gen.bounty.0.done.1: Take the reward. The cheese is mine.
dlg.gen.bounty.1.offer.0: There is a wedding on Saturday. The bride's family is rich, the groom's family is armed, and {target} are loitering on the road.
dlg.gen.bounty.1.offer.1: Clear {count} {target} before then. A quiet road makes a quiet wedding. A bloody one costs extra.
dlg.gen.bounty.1.more.0: Last year a Pulse moved the groom to the wrong village. They married anyway. Love is stubborn. So is the seating plan.
dlg.gen.bounty.1.more.1: Come to the feast after, if you like. Free soup. Do not ask whose.
dlg.gen.bounty.1.wait.0: Saturday gets closer. The road does not get clearer. The bride's mother has started speaking to me directly.
dlg.gen.bounty.1.done.0: The road is clear! The bride's mother has stopped speaking to me, which is the best result I could hope for.
dlg.gen.bounty.1.done.1: Here is your reward. The soup offer stands. The answer to whose is still no.
dlg.gen.bounty.2.offer.0: The tax collector went out to the farms three days ago. The taxes came back. The collector did not.
dlg.gen.bounty.2.offer.1: {target} roam that stretch. Kill {count} and see what turns up. Preferably the collector. Failing that, the taxes.
dlg.gen.bounty.2.more.0: Nobody liked him. Everyone wants him found. That is the nature of a debt: you only miss it once it is gone.
dlg.gen.bounty.2.more.1: If you find him alive, he will want a receipt. If not, he will want one anyway. It is who he was.
dlg.gen.bounty.2.wait.0: No collector yet. The farmers have gone suspiciously cheerful. I am keeping an eye on them.
dlg.gen.bounty.2.done.0: We found his hat. And his ledger, chewed. The farms are lighter by one debt, the town by one pest. I cannot say which loss hurts less.
dlg.gen.bounty.2.done.1: Your reward. It comes out of the tax fund, which is now technically a memorial fund.
dlg.gen.bounty.3.offer.0: A kid wandered off into the fields. Came back two days later. Polite. Washed. Said 'please' twice.
dlg.gen.bounty.3.offer.1: Something out there did it, and {target} were the only company. Kill {count}. I would like the rest of the village to stay rude.
dlg.gen.bounty.3.more.0: The parents are thrilled and terrified. They keep asking me whether to be proud or to bar the door.
dlg.gen.bounty.3.more.1: It is probably a Pulse. It is probably fine. I have said 'probably' so often it has stopped meaning anything.
dlg.gen.bounty.3.wait.0: The kid brought me tea. I did not ask for tea. Please hurry.
dlg.gen.bounty.3.done.0: The kid sneezed, burped, and called me a rude name. Back to normal. I have never been so happy to be insulted.
dlg.gen.bounty.3.done.1: Here is the reward. Thank you. Do not mention the tea to the parents.
dlg.gen.patrol.0.offer.0: The walls hold. My people hold. The wilds do not care either way, and they have been creeping closer to {here}.
dlg.gen.patrol.0.offer.1: Thin out {count} of anything out there. Anything with teeth, claws, or a strong opinion of us.
dlg.gen.patrol.0.more.0: A patrol is mostly walking. Walking is mostly boredom. The boredom is occasionally interrupted by teeth.
dlg.gen.patrol.0.wait.0: Patrol is not done. I have the count right here. It says 'not enough'.
dlg.gen.patrol.0.done.0: Safer already. By one patrol's worth, at least. I can almost hear the guards relax.
dlg.gen.patrol.0.done.1: Your reward. You did what they pay us to do, with fewer complaints about the pay.
dlg.gen.patrol.1.offer.0: My guards are tired. My guards are also frightened. Both are my fault, so I have decided to blame the weather.
dlg.gen.patrol.1.offer.1: Take down {count} monsters of any kind near {here}. Do it for the guards. Do it for the weather.
dlg.gen.patrol.1.more.0: They have stood the same watch for a week. One asked for a transfer to the fishing village. Then he remembered he cannot swim.
dlg.gen.patrol.1.wait.0: The guards are still tired. Could you make them less tired? Preferably by killing things.
dlg.gen.patrol.1.done.0: My guards slept in shifts last night. Real shifts. Not the kind that rewrite the world.
dlg.gen.patrol.1.done.1: Take the reward and the thanks. The thanks are cheaper, but sincere.
dlg.gen.patrol.2.offer.0: Inspection day. I am told a lord may visit {here}. I am told this by a man who also told me the moon was cheese.
dlg.gen.patrol.2.offer.1: I would like the surroundings tidy. {count} of anything unfriendly, out of sight. Tidy is a state of mind, but fewer teeth help.
dlg.gen.patrol.2.more.0: If the lord comes, he will bring clerks. Clerks ask questions. Dead monsters cannot answer them. That is the point.
dlg.gen.patrol.2.more.1: If he does not come, you made the road safer for nothing. In this job that is called a good day.
dlg.gen.patrol.2.wait.0: Still messy out there. I can see it from the tower. It is looking back.
dlg.gen.patrol.2.done.0: Tidy! The lord did not come. Neither did the clerks. Neither did the monsters. A complete success.
dlg.gen.patrol.2.done.1: Your reward. The gratitude is a bonus. Have it framed.
dlg.gen.patrol.3.offer.0: My guards have a pool going: how many monsters you will kill before you run. I have money on 'quite a few'.
dlg.gen.patrol.3.offer.1: Prove me right. {count} of anything around {here}. The winnings go to the house. The reward goes to you.
dlg.gen.patrol.3.more.0: It is a harmless pool. A little morbid. We run another on how long the elder keeps his hat.
dlg.gen.patrol.3.more.1: Do not tell the lieutenant. He bet on 'none'.
dlg.gen.patrol.3.wait.0: The lieutenant keeps looking at me and smiling. He thinks he is winning. Show him otherwise.
dlg.gen.patrol.3.done.0: I win! The lieutenant owes me a month of night duty. Also, you are a good soldier. In that order.
dlg.gen.patrol.3.done.1: Your reward. Spend it before the lieutenant tries to bet it off you.
dlg.gen.courier.0.offer.0: Everybody here has someone out there. This one has a debt in {town}. Small, embarrassing, old.
dlg.gen.courier.0.offer.1: Take this letter to the innkeeper there. Do not read it. I did, and it was uncomfortable.
dlg.gen.courier.0.more.0: It is the money for a dinner eaten twelve years ago. His honour has finally caught up with his belly.
dlg.gen.courier.0.more.1: The man has dreamed about that dinner for twelve years. Deliver it before he dies of the memory.
dlg.gen.courier.0.wait.0: Letter still in your pack? Good. Debts get lighter when carried and heavier when read.
dlg.gen.courier.0.done.0: A letter for me? Oh. The soup man. Twelve years, and he still owes me for the soup.
dlg.gen.courier.0.done.1: He paid! Well. Forgive the interest. The soup was bad anyway. Here is something for your trouble.
dlg.gen.courier.1.offer.0: A letter for someone in {town}. Perfumed, sealed, written four times. The first three drafts were worse, and I read them all.
dlg.gen.courier.1.offer.1: Hand it to the innkeeper there. Try not to look romantic while you do it. You will fail, but try.
dlg.gen.courier.1.more.0: He has been writing it since the last Pulse. The Pulse changed his handwriting twice and the poem once.
dlg.gen.courier.1.wait.0: Is the letter still dry? It is a love letter. Keep it dry, and far from open flame. And from me.
dlg.gen.courier.1.done.0: A letter! It is from him. He is alive. And still terrible at poetry. He rhymes 'heart' with 'cart' again.
dlg.gen.courier.1.done.1: Tell him yes. No, tell him I will think about it. No, tell him yes. Here, for your trouble.
dlg.gen.courier.2.offer.0: An old customer died. Not suddenly. He prepared. Hence a will, written very carefully and signed three times.
dlg.gen.courier.2.offer.1: It goes to his niece, at the inn in {town}. Take it there. If the roads kill you, I will draw up a will for you too.
dlg.gen.courier.2.more.0: He left me his hat and one instruction: 'Do not wear the hat.' I am still deciding what it means.
dlg.gen.courier.2.more.1: The will mentions a debt, a goat and a fold in the road. I am not asking.
dlg.gen.courier.2.wait.0: The will is heavier than it looks. They always are. Please do not die with it. The paperwork would be dreadful.
dlg.gen.courier.2.done.0: My uncle's will? Oh. He finally did it. I would say rest in peace, but he never could, not with that hat.
dlg.gen.courier.2.done.1: Thank you for bringing it. Here is something for your trouble. It is not in the will, so do not tell the lawyers.
dlg.gen.courier.3.offer.0: An apology. Three Pulses late, which in this world means nobody remembers what it was for.
dlg.gen.courier.3.offer.1: It is for the innkeeper in {town}. The sender hopes it arrives before he remembers what he did.
dlg.gen.courier.3.more.0: He wrote it after a Pulse took his memory. Everything in it is guesswork: 'I am sorry for whatever I did.'
dlg.gen.courier.3.more.1: It is a good letter. Short. Honest. Neither of us has any idea what it is about.
dlg.gen.courier.3.wait.0: Still carrying it? Good. The sooner it arrives, the sooner someone gets to be angry about it.
dlg.gen.courier.3.done.0: An apology? From him? For what? I cannot recall either. Some Pulse took the quarrel and left the guilt.
dlg.gen.courier.3.done.1: Well. I accept it anyway. Tell him we are even. Here is something for you, for the walk.
dlg.gen.boss.0.offer.0: {target} has been seen again. Closer to the road than last time. Closer to my guards than I like.
dlg.gen.boss.0.offer.1: Slay it. I have been saying 'someone should' for a month. You are someone, which is a promotion.
dlg.gen.boss.0.more.0: The bounty has been posted since the last Pulse. Three have tried. One was my cousin. He was a good cousin.
dlg.gen.boss.0.more.1: It has a lair, and it keeps to it. Find it, and finish it, before it finishes us.
dlg.gen.boss.0.wait.0: Is it dead yet? I will know when the guards cheer. So far the guards are very quiet.
dlg.gen.boss.0.done.0: The guards cheered. Quietly, then loudly, then somebody fainted. A good day.
dlg.gen.boss.0.done.1: Slain! I will write it up. The ledger will say you did it, and I will say I helped. The reward is yours.
dlg.gen.boss.1.offer.0: Every few months something rises that should not. This season it is {target}, and it has been eating the trade route.
dlg.gen.boss.1.offer.1: Merchants refuse to travel. That is good for my quiet and bad for my pay. Kill it, and I get both back.
dlg.gen.boss.1.more.0: The merchants gave it a name. They always do. It makes the losses easier to write down.
dlg.gen.boss.1.more.1: Bring proof, or at least a good story. I accept either.
dlg.gen.boss.1.wait.0: The merchants keep asking when the road opens. I keep saying 'soon'. I am running out of ways to say it.
dlg.gen.boss.1.done.0: The road is open! Merchants are weeping, in a good way. Someone is already selling souvenirs. I have no comment.
dlg.gen.boss.1.done.1: Take the reward, and as many souvenirs as you can carry. I bought one. It is already breaking.
dlg.gen.boss.2.offer.0: I am tired of funerals. I have attended nine this year, and only one was for someone I liked.
dlg.gen.boss.2.offer.1: {target} is behind most of them. Kill it, and I might finally have an evening to myself.
dlg.gen.boss.2.more.0: It is big. Everything out there is big, but this one is big on purpose. You will know it when it looks down at you.
dlg.gen.boss.2.more.1: Bring friends if you have them. Come back alone if you must. Come back regardless.
dlg.gen.boss.2.wait.0: Another funeral on the calendar. Not yours, I hope. Is it dead yet?
dlg.gen.boss.2.done.0: No funeral this week. First time since spring. I spent the evening staring at a wall and loving it.
dlg.gen.boss.2.done.1: Your reward. And my thanks. Spend it somewhere with a good roof.
dlg.gen.boss.3.offer.0: My oldest guard says {target} was here before the wall. He also says the wall was here before the moon. He is not reliable.
dlg.gen.boss.3.offer.1: Reliable or not, the beast is real. It is near, and it is angry. Put it down.
dlg.gen.boss.3.more.0: He fought it twice. He says it remembers him. I say that is the ale.
dlg.gen.boss.3.more.1: If it does remember you, it will not be fond. Be quick.
dlg.gen.boss.3.wait.0: My old guard keeps asking if you are back. He wants to know if it still remembers him.
dlg.gen.boss.3.done.0: He wept when I told him. Said he had waited thirty years. Then he asked for a drink, and I gave him two.
dlg.gen.boss.3.done.1: Your reward. And a little respect from an old man who has fought less than you.
dlg.gen.dungeon.0.offer.0: Child, something below does not pray. It does not sleep, either. It has taken the {dungeon} for its own.
dlg.gen.dungeon.0.offer.1: Go down. Defeat what rules it. I would go myself, but my knees have a more reasonable faith than I do.
dlg.gen.dungeon.0.more.0: Old-world places keep old-world things. The Palm does not reach them. We must be the hand that does.
dlg.gen.dungeon.0.more.1: Bless yourself first. It does nothing, but I find it calming. The Palm will do the rest.
dlg.gen.dungeon.0.wait.0: Down in the {dungeon}, then. I pray for you. Out loud, so the flock thinks I am busy.
dlg.gen.dungeon.0.done.0: The sermon will be easier this week. Fewer screams from below. Thank you, child.
dlg.gen.dungeon.0.done.1: The Palm holds us, and you held the door. Take the reward. Spend it on something unholy, if you must.
dlg.gen.dungeon.1.offer.0: The faithful keep going down into the {dungeon}. Few come back. Those who do ask for refunds.
dlg.gen.dungeon.1.offer.1: Defeat what rules it, so I can stop writing eulogies. I am running out of synonyms for 'unfortunate'.
dlg.gen.dungeon.1.more.0: I have used 'taken', 'lost', 'misplaced', and 'consumed by an unspecified fold'. The last sounds best.
dlg.gen.dungeon.1.more.1: Go in with courage. Come out with the reward. In between, go with some sense.
dlg.gen.dungeon.1.wait.0: I still keep a eulogy for you in the drawer. I would love to burn it.
dlg.gen.dungeon.1.done.0: I am tearing up the eulogy. It was one of my best, too. Such a waste.
dlg.gen.dungeon.1.done.1: The reward is yours. May the Palm always be warm under your boots.
dlg.gen.dungeon.2.offer.0: I had a dream. A voice below the {dungeon} asked for someone to mind the door. I woke to find my sandals by the cellar stairs.
dlg.gen.dungeon.2.offer.1: I am not brave. You, I think, are. Go down. Defeat what rules there, and let the voice sleep.
dlg.gen.dungeon.2.more.0: A Pulse may have sent the dream. A Pulse may have sent the sandals. I no longer rule out that the Palm has a sense of humour.
dlg.gen.dungeon.2.more.1: If the voice asks you for something, say no. If it asks politely, say no politely.
dlg.gen.dungeon.2.wait.0: The voice asked again last night. Politely. It is very annoying.
dlg.gen.dungeon.2.done.0: I slept! A full night. No voice, no sandals. I almost wept.
dlg.gen.dungeon.2.done.1: Take the reward, and a blessing. A legitimate one this time. I checked.
dlg.gen.dungeon.3.offer.0: Whatever rules the {dungeon} was a person once. It had a name and a post. The name is gone. It still keeps the post.
dlg.gen.dungeon.3.offer.1: Defeat it. Not because it is evil, but because it is no longer who it was. Mercy by other means.
dlg.gen.dungeon.3.more.0: Grandmothers say those houses shut with their keepers inside. This one has kept its watch for three hundred years. That wears a person down.
dlg.gen.dungeon.3.more.1: Do it kindly, if the sword allows.
dlg.gen.dungeon.3.wait.0: I pray for it too, you know. Whatever rules the {dungeon}. A short prayer. The Palm is not always listening.
dlg.gen.dungeon.3.done.0: Its watch is over at last. Poor soul. Three hundred years is a long time to wait for someone to take over.
dlg.gen.dungeon.3.done.1: Your reward, with my gratitude. I will say a word for both of you tonight.
dlg.gen.bounty.elder.0.offer.0: I am the elder, the baker, and the one who knows where the shovels are. Today I am also the man who needs {target} gone.
dlg.gen.bounty.elder.0.offer.1: {count} should do. We cannot afford more. We cannot afford these either, but here we are.
dlg.gen.bounty.elder.0.more.0: My crops are thin and my guards are me. I am not asking for glory. Only for the fields.
dlg.gen.bounty.elder.0.wait.0: Still out there? I can hear them from the barn. The cow can too. She has opinions.
dlg.gen.bounty.elder.0.done.0: Thank you. The cow can sleep, and so can I. Do not tell the others I wept a little.
dlg.gen.bounty.elder.0.done.1: Here is what we can spare. It is not much. It is all of it.
dlg.gen.bounty.elder.1.offer.0: My wife said, 'Marry a farmer, he will not need heroes.' I became the elder instead. Here we are.
dlg.gen.bounty.elder.1.offer.1: {count} {target} are at the fence again. Deal with them, and I will tell her you were charming.
dlg.gen.bounty.elder.1.more.0: We have no captain here. We have a fence, a dog, and good intentions. The dog has retired.
dlg.gen.bounty.elder.1.wait.0: The fence is still holding. The dog is not. Please be quick.
dlg.gen.bounty.elder.1.done.0: Quiet at the fence. The dog is back on duty. He seems smug.
dlg.gen.bounty.elder.1.done.1: Take the reward. And my thanks, which is all I have left of the first kind.
dlg.gen.patrol.elder.0.offer.0: No captain here. No guards either. There is me, and a rake. We have not been formally introduced to the monsters.
dlg.gen.patrol.elder.0.offer.1: Thin out {count} of anything around {here}. We will sleep better. Or sleep at all.
dlg.gen.patrol.elder.0.more.0: Every night I hear them walk the edge. Not attack. Just walk. As if they were counting the doors.
dlg.gen.patrol.elder.0.wait.0: I heard them again. Fewer? I think fewer. I am an optimist. It is the last thing I own.
dlg.gen.patrol.elder.0.done.0: Fewer footsteps tonight. I counted. It is what I do now.
dlg.gen.patrol.elder.0.done.1: Here is the reward. Thank you for walking where I cannot.
dlg.gen.patrol.elder.1.offer.0: The children are not allowed beyond the well. The children do not understand. Neither do the monsters. Nobody respects a line.
dlg.gen.patrol.elder.1.offer.1: Clear {count} of anything near {here}, so that the line can finally mean something.
dlg.gen.patrol.elder.1.more.0: I drew that line myself, with a stick. It is a good line. Help me make it a rule.
dlg.gen.patrol.elder.1.wait.0: The line holds, mostly. The children test it hourly. So do the monsters.
dlg.gen.patrol.elder.1.done.0: The line holds. The children think it is magic. Let them. I do not mind being a wizard.
dlg.gen.patrol.elder.1.done.1: Your reward, and the village's thanks. We have little else, but we do have thanks.
dlg.gen.courier.elder.0.offer.0: A recipe. My late wife's. She wrote it for her sister in {town}, and then, being her, left it unsent for ten years.
dlg.gen.courier.elder.0.offer.1: Take it there. Find the innkeeper, they will know where the sister is. Or pretend to, which is nearly as good.
dlg.gen.courier.elder.0.more.0: It is only a stew. It is the stew that made me marry her. It deserves a better messenger than I, but you are what I have.
dlg.gen.courier.elder.0.wait.0: Recipe still with you? Good. Keep it from the damp. And from your own hunger.
dlg.gen.courier.elder.0.done.0: A recipe? Oh. That is her handwriting. She always crossed her sevens, like a clerk with a grudge.
dlg.gen.courier.elder.0.done.1: I will take it to her sister. She will cry. Then she will cook. Here, something for the walk.
dlg.gen.courier.elder.1.offer.0: A parcel for {town}. It hums when you hold it. I have stopped holding it. It is wrapped in cloth and a bad feeling.
dlg.gen.courier.elder.1.offer.1: It came with the last Pulse, addressed to someone there. Even a Pulse has manners. Take it, and do not unwrap it.
dlg.gen.courier.elder.1.more.0: If it hums louder, put it down. If it hums a tune, run. If you recognise the tune, come and tell me.
dlg.gen.courier.elder.1.wait.0: Still humming? Good. It means it has not gone off. Hold it like a loaf.
dlg.gen.courier.elder.1.done.0: That hum! I have waited all season. Finally. Was it loud on the road? Sorry.
dlg.gen.courier.elder.1.done.1: It is mine, I am nearly sure. Do not ask what it is. Here, for your trouble and your hearing.
dlg.gen.boss.elder.0.offer.0: I am the elder, which means I must be the one to say it: {target} has come near, and we cannot fight it.
dlg.gen.boss.elder.0.offer.1: We have pitchforks, prayers, and a debt to the miller. None of it works on a thing like that. Please, slay it.
dlg.gen.boss.elder.0.more.0: I will not lie. People have died. I know all of their names. It is the one thing I can still do.
dlg.gen.boss.elder.0.wait.0: I keep the names on a board by the gate. If you need to add yours, I will spell it right. Once I know it.
dlg.gen.boss.elder.0.done.0: It is over. I am taking the board down. Slowly. I want to enjoy it.
dlg.gen.boss.elder.0.done.1: The reward is yours. The village's gratitude is longer, but heavier to carry.
dlg.gen.boss.elder.1.offer.0: We are a small place with a small hope. It has been smaller since {target} arrived.
dlg.gen.boss.elder.1.offer.1: Kill it. I would offer more, but an offer is all I have. And the reward, which is real.
dlg.gen.boss.elder.1.more.0: I could write to the capital. The capital would write back. By then I would be a memory, or a different elder.
dlg.gen.boss.elder.1.wait.0: Still waiting. It is good for me, I am told. Patience builds character. Mine is finished.
dlg.gen.boss.elder.1.done.0: We live! What a surprise. I had written my resignation, just in case. I will keep it for the next one.
dlg.gen.boss.elder.1.done.1: Please take the reward. We have nothing finer, but it is what we have.
dlg.gen.dungeon.elder.0.offer.0: Our priest left for the next village. Nobody knows why. The {dungeon} below has been louder since.
dlg.gen.dungeon.elder.0.offer.1: Go down. Defeat what rules it. I would go, but I have a hip, a harvest, and a deeply held cowardice.
dlg.gen.dungeon.elder.0.more.0: It is an old-world place. Nothing prays there. Nothing sleeps there either. That is the part that bothers me.
dlg.gen.dungeon.elder.0.wait.0: If you hear noises from below, that is me, praying for you. Badly.
dlg.gen.dungeon.elder.0.done.0: It is quiet down there. The ground has stopped humming at me. I forgot how much I hated that.
dlg.gen.dungeon.elder.0.done.1: Take the reward. And if you meet the priest, tell him he has missed nothing.
dlg.gen.dungeon.elder.1.offer.0: Every autumn the {dungeon} wakes. We used to feed it goats. This year the goats have started to talk, and refuse.
dlg.gen.dungeon.elder.1.offer.1: So I am asking you instead. Go down, defeat what rules it. You are cheaper than a goat, and you can talk back.
dlg.gen.dungeon.elder.1.more.0: I am told it never needed the goats. We just thought it did. Old habits are expensive.
dlg.gen.dungeon.elder.1.wait.0: The goats are watching the path. Waiting to see if you come back. So am I.
dlg.gen.dungeon.elder.1.done.0: The ground is quiet. The goats are grazing. One of them winked at me. I will try not to think about it.
dlg.gen.dungeon.elder.1.done.1: Your reward. We owe you more, but we have little, and the goats refuse to pay.
dlg.reply.accept.1: Consider it done. Or at least scheduled.
dlg.reply.accept.2: Fine. Put me down for it.
dlg.reply.accept.3: Overtime it is. I'll do it.
dlg.reply.accept.4: Sign me up. Is there a form?
dlg.reply.accept.7: All right. I'll go and look.
dlg.reply.more.2: Is there a safety briefing first?
dlg.reply.more.3: What am I not being told?
dlg.reply.decline.1: Maybe later. I need a minute.
dlg.reply.decline.3: I have a shift report to finish.
dlg.reply.turnin.1: Job finished. Where do I sign?
dlg.reply.turnin.3: All done. Let's call it a shift.
dlg.reply.turnin.4: That's that. I'll take the reward.
dlg.reply.turnin.5: Done. Try not to look so surprised.
dlg.decline.elder.0: Of course. The wells will still be here. Probably.
dlg.decline.elder.1: Take your time. Time is the one thing we have plenty of, thanks to the Pulse.
dlg.decline.priest.0: The Palm waits, child. It is very patient. I am less so, but I try.
dlg.decline.priest.1: Go in peace. And come back in one piece, ideally.
dlg.decline.captain.0: Fine. The monsters will wait. They always do. It is their one virtue.
dlg.decline.captain.1: No pressure. Only teeth. Come back when you are ready.
dlg.decline.innkeeper.0: No rush. The letter will keep. Mostly.
dlg.decline.innkeeper.1: Another time, then. Have a drink while you are here. On the house. Well, for a price.
dlg.decline.chronicler.0: Another time. History is patient, though it does get revised.
dlg.decline.chronicler.1: Think it over. The past is not going anywhere, which is rather the problem.
dlg.decline.ruler.0: Think it over. The kingdom has waited three centuries. It can spare a day.
dlg.decline.ruler.1: Take your time. The crown is heavy, but it will not run off.
dlg.ask.trouble.0: You look like something went wrong.
dlg.ask.trouble.2: Trouble? I know that face. I used to wear it.
dlg.ask.else.1: What else keeps you up at night?
dlg.ask.else.2: And the other problem? There is always another.
dlg.ask.place.1: What should a stranger know here?
dlg.ask.bye.1: I should go. Things to kill.
dlg.ask.bye.2: Back to my shift. So to speak.
dlg.q_gate_1.offer.0: Old Hesk was on the gate the morning you came out. Since then he watches the fold, not the road.
dlg.q_gate_1.offer.1: The road has noticed. Wolves walked right up to the gate yesterday. Thin out {count} {target} while he stares at nothing.
dlg.q_gate_1.more.0: I told him the fold lets someone out once a generation. He said he is not leaving before the next generation.
dlg.q_gate_1.more.1: He has not slept since. Ask him why, and he will tell you about the weather.
dlg.q_gate_1.wait.0: Hesk is still watching. Wolves are still walking. Only one of those is my job.
dlg.q_gate_1.done.0: Quieter on the road. Hesk did not notice. He asked me whether you came out feet first or head first.
dlg.q_gate_1.done.1: I said I was not looking. He wrote 'unknown' in a little book. Here is your pay.
dlg.q_gate_2.offer.0: Hesk has strung a fishing net across the gate. To catch the next one, he says. So far it catches bats.
dlg.q_gate_2.offer.1: The bats are angry and the carters are tangled. Kill {count} {target} before somebody else gets caught.
dlg.q_gate_2.more.0: Forty years ago the fold let out goats. Hesk had the watch. Hesk was asleep. The goats walked past him into the market.
dlg.q_gate_2.more.1: On feast days the whole town still bleats at him. He laughs along. He does not laugh much otherwise.
dlg.q_gate_2.wait.0: Another carter in the net this morning. He wants to file a complaint. I have asked him to hold still.
dlg.q_gate_2.done.0: Fewer bats. The net is mended. Hesk has tied a bell to it, in case he blinks.
dlg.q_gate_2.done.1: Your pay. If the bell rings at night, it is not my problem. It is his. Mostly his.
dlg.q_gate_3.offer.0: The bell rang at midnight. Something came out of the fold, tore through the net and ran. Hesk went after it with a rope and a lantern.
dlg.q_gate_3.offer.1: He is old, and the dark is full of teeth. Clear {count} of anything out there. Quickly, please.
dlg.q_gate_3.more.0: He left his spear behind. He said whatever comes out of a fold is frightened, and you do not spear the frightened.
dlg.q_gate_3.more.1: He said that about you, too. I was going to spear you. Thank him, if you find him.
dlg.q_gate_3.reply.accept: Rope, lantern, old man. On my way.
dlg.q_gate_3.wait.0: I can see his lantern from the wall. It is still moving. That is good.
dlg.q_eel_1.offer.0: The eel from the north well lives in my font now. A child put it there. The child has been forgiven. The eel was not asked.
dlg.q_eel_1.offer.1: Slime keeps creeping up from the well to visit it. Kill {count} {target} before they reach the altar.
dlg.q_eel_1.more.0: It came up the well after a Pulse. No river we know claims it. It eats bread and listens to the sermon.
dlg.q_eel_1.more.1: It listens better than the flock. I am not proud of saying that. I am saying it.
dlg.q_eel_1.wait.0: Slime on the steps again. The eel watched it come in. It did not blink. I am not sure it can.
dlg.q_eel_1.done.0: The steps are clean. The eel has had its bread. So have I. We are both calmer.
dlg.q_eel_1.done.1: Your reward. If you pass the font, nod to it. It likes that.
dlg.q_eel_2.offer.0: Word got out. People walk in from the hamlets to see the eel. Some kneel. I have asked them not to. The eel has said nothing.
dlg.q_eel_2.offer.1: The roads are not safe for people on their knees. Clear {count} of anything on the way, so they arrive in one piece.
dlg.q_eel_2.more.0: A woman says it cured her cough. A man says it looked at him and he forgave his brother. I say it is an eel.
dlg.q_eel_2.more.1: The collection plate has never been fuller. That is the part that worries me.
dlg.q_eel_2.wait.0: More pilgrims today. One brought the eel a hat. The eel is wearing the hat. Nobody knows how.
dlg.q_eel_2.done.0: The roads are quieter. The pilgrims arrive dry-eyed and leave wet-eyed. The eel remains an eel.
dlg.q_eel_2.done.1: Your reward, from the collection plate. The Palm can spare it. So can the eel.
dlg.q_eel_3.offer.0: The eel is gone. The font is empty. The pilgrims have not noticed, or they have, and kneel anyway.
dlg.q_eel_3.offer.1: Meanwhile the north well is thick with slime again. Kill {count} {target} there. Do not ask why the well. Just the well.
dlg.q_eel_3.more.0: It stopped eating on Tuesday. It lay at the bottom of the bowl and looked at the ceiling. I know that look. I have worn it.
dlg.q_eel_3.more.1: Someone must have taken it in the night. There are thieves everywhere. I lock the church. Mostly.
dlg.q_eel_3.wait.0: Is the well clear yet? I ask for no reason. A priest may ask about a well.
dlg.q_cellar_1.offer.0: Bats in my cellar. They come through a crack in the back wall. The crack was not there before the last Pulse.
dlg.q_cellar_1.offer.1: Kill {count} {target} for me, quietly. And not a word about the crack. People talk, and then they drink elsewhere.
dlg.q_cellar_1.more.0: I put a barrel against it. The barrel is now on the other side of the crack. I did not see it go.
dlg.q_cellar_1.more.1: It is a small crack. A small tear, the elder would say. I do not say that word in my own cellar.
dlg.q_cellar_1.wait.0: Still bats. I pour with one hand and hold a broom in the other. It is good for tips.
dlg.q_cellar_1.done.0: No bats. The cellar is quiet. Too quiet for a cellar, but I will take it.
dlg.q_cellar_1.done.1: Here is your pay. Remember: there is no crack. Have a drink.
dlg.q_cellar_2.offer.0: The barrel came back through the crack last night. Full. Not of beer.
dlg.q_cellar_2.offer.1: The slime got out and went off toward the mill. Kill {count} {target} before the miller tells us the flour is fine.
dlg.q_cellar_2.more.0: I have served worse things out of that barrel. Not much worse. Do not tell anyone that either.
dlg.q_cellar_2.more.1: The crack is a little wider. I hung a curtain over it. A nice curtain. The only nice thing down there.
dlg.q_cellar_2.wait.0: The miller came in for a drink. He says the flour is fine. He had slime on his boots.
dlg.q_cellar_3.offer.0: Good news. I sell tickets to the cellar now. One copper to look at the crack. Two to put your hand near it.
dlg.q_cellar_3.offer.1: People walk in from three hamlets, and the roads are not safe for people who pay me. Clear {count} of anything, please.
dlg.q_cellar_3.more.0: Yes, I said keep it quiet. That was before I counted what quiet was costing me.
dlg.q_cellar_3.more.1: A man put his whole arm in. It came back fine. Longer, he says. He paid double to say so.
dlg.q_cellar_3.wait.0: The queue goes up the stairs and out the door. The roads are still full of teeth. One of those has to change.
dlg.q_cellar_3.done.0: Roads clear, cellar full. If the world ends, it will start in my cellar, and I will be selling tickets.
dlg.q_cellar_3.done.1: Your share. Do not call it a share in front of the priest.
dlg.q_cellar_3.reply.turnin: Done. Do I get a free look?
dlg.q_gate_3.done.0: He is back. Soaked, scratched and grinning. On the end of his rope there is a goat.
dlg.q_gate_3.done.1: He was awake for this one, he says. He has named her Wanderer.
dlg.q_gate_3.done.2: The elder says nothing from a fold may sleep inside the wall. You came out of one too, so they will take your word. Does she stay?
dlg.q_gate_3.choice.keep: She stays. I came out of a fold too.
dlg.q_gate_3.choice.free: Let her go. Hesk can walk her out.
dlg.q_gate_3.chosen.keep.0: Then she stays. The elder will complain. I will let him.
dlg.q_gate_3.chosen.keep.1: Hesk has not stopped grinning. Somebody find him a pen for her before she eats the gate.
dlg.q_gate_3.chosen.keep.2: Your pay. If the elder sends you a bill for the goat, do not pay it.
dlg.q_gate_3.chosen.free.0: Then she goes. Hesk will walk her out himself. He did not ask for company.
dlg.q_gate_3.chosen.free.1: He took her as far as the last field and came back without the rope.
dlg.q_gate_3.chosen.free.2: Your pay. And this is his spear. He said to give it to the one who chose. I do not know if that is thanks.
dlg.q_gate_3.after.keep.0: Hesk sleeps now. In the goat pen. He says it is quieter there.
dlg.q_gate_3.after.keep.1: The bread went wrong this week. The town blames the goat. The goat has not commented.
dlg.q_gate_3.after.keep.2: The elder still says she must go. She eats his notices off the hall door. I think it is personal.
dlg.q_gate_3.after.free.0: Hesk walks out to the last field every morning. She is always there. He takes bread.
dlg.q_gate_3.after.free.1: No wolves by the last field lately. There is a goat out there. I have stopped asking questions.
dlg.q_gate_3.after.free.2: Hesk is back on the gate. He watches the field now, not the fold. It is an improvement.
dlg.q_eel_3.done.0: The well is clear. If you look down at dusk, something looks back up.
dlg.q_eel_3.done.1: The pilgrims ask me where the eel went. I have told them nothing yet. Telling nothing is a skill. I have been practising.
dlg.q_eel_3.done.2: You were at the well. What did you see? Whatever you say, that is what I will tell them.
dlg.q_eel_3.choice.tell: Your eel. Tell them where it is.
dlg.q_eel_3.chosen.hide.0: Just water. Yes. That is what I saw too.
dlg.q_eel_3.chosen.hide.1: Then the bowl stays empty, and they keep kneeling to it. The Palm will forgive me. I will see how I do.
dlg.q_eel_3.chosen.hide.2: Your reward, from the plate. It is very full.
dlg.q_eel_3.chosen.tell.0: ...Yes. I carried it there myself, on Tuesday night, in the bowl, under my robe. I did not drop it.
dlg.q_eel_3.chosen.tell.1: I will tell them on Sunday. They will go to the well. Nobody will draw water in peace again.
dlg.q_eel_3.chosen.tell.2: Your reward. Take it now, before the plate is empty. It will be empty soon.
dlg.q_eel_3.after.hide.0: The bowl is still empty. I polish it every morning. It is the least I can do, and I do the least.
dlg.q_eel_3.after.hide.1: Someone leaves bread at the north well. Nobody saw who. I did not see either.
dlg.q_eel_3.after.hide.2: Attendance has never been better. I preach on honesty now. The flock says it is my best work.
dlg.q_eel_3.after.tell.0: Since Sunday the pilgrims kneel at the north well. You have to step over them to fetch water.
dlg.q_eel_3.after.tell.1: The plate is empty and the roof leaks. I sleep well. Most nights that is a fair trade.
dlg.q_eel_3.after.tell.2: It has not shown itself since the crowds came. I go to the well at dusk anyway. Alone.
dlg.q_cellar_2.done.0: The mill road is clear. Last night something behind the curtain moved it to one side. Politely.
dlg.q_cellar_2.done.1: The crack is as wide as a door now. The mason can wall it up with anchor stone, at a price that makes me sit down. He comes once.
dlg.q_cellar_2.done.2: Wall it up, and someone must keep the bats off the mason. Leave it, and my guests need safe roads. Stone, once set, stays set.
dlg.q_cellar_2.choice.seal: Wall it up. I'll keep the bats off the mason.
dlg.q_cellar_2.choice.sell: Leave it open. I'll clear the roads for guests.
dlg.q_cellar_2.chosen.seal.0: Wall it up. Yes. I will send for the mason and ask the elder for a block of stone.
dlg.q_cellar_2.chosen.seal.1: He will want it paid the old way. Nothing in this town comes cheap if it is grey and warm.
dlg.q_cellar_2.chosen.seal.2: Your pay, and a drink. I need two.
dlg.q_cellar_2.chosen.sell.0: Good for business. Yes. That is what I keep telling myself in the dark.
dlg.q_cellar_2.chosen.sell.1: I will need a sign. And a curtain in a better colour. And a man on the stairs.
dlg.q_cellar_2.chosen.sell.2: Your pay, and a free drink. Come back tomorrow. I may have something for you.
dlg.q_cellar_2.after.seal.0: One block of anchor stone in my cellar wall. A year of profit. Cheap, for sleep.
dlg.q_cellar_2.after.seal.1: Every Sunday something knocks twice behind the new block. Politely. I knock back. It would be rude not to.
dlg.q_cellar_2.after.seal.2: The inn owes the wall now. The wall is a patient creditor. I am not used to this side of the counter.
dlg.q_cellar_2.after.sell.0: Tickets at the door. A look is one copper. A hand near it is two. An arm, we discuss.
dlg.q_cellar_2.after.sell.1: Some nights the curtain moves on its own. The customers love it. I have stopped going down after dark.
dlg.q_cellar_2.after.sell.2: Business has never been this good. I sleep with the lamp on.
dlg.q_cellar_3b.offer.0: The elder gave me one block of anchor stone. The price is in his ledger. I have not dared to read it.
dlg.q_cellar_3b.offer.1: The mason started this morning. At the first brick, everything behind the curtain flew out. Kill {count} {target} so he can finish.
dlg.q_cellar_3b.more.0: The elder says stone is paid in stone or in blood. I have neither. So I am paying in you. Sorry.
dlg.q_cellar_3b.more.1: The mason is not afraid. The mason is deaf. From the stairs they look the same.
dlg.q_cellar_3b.wait.0: The mason has set half the block. The bats have set up in the rafters. Please.
dlg.q_cellar_3b.reply.turnin: Done. Does the barrel stay put now?
dlg.q_cellar_3b.done.0: It is done. One grey block in my cellar wall. Warm to the touch. Quieter than a wall has any right to be.
dlg.q_cellar_3b.done.1: I put the barrel against it. The barrel stayed. Here is your pay. Less than I would like. More than I have.
dlg.q_eel_3.if.q_gate_3.keep.0: And the flock has a new member. The goat from the gate comes to the sermon now. She stays to the end. Few do.
dlg.q_eel_3.if.q_gate_3.free.0: One more thing for the flock to whisper about: Hesk came to church, first time in years, and asked the Palm about a goat.
dlg.q_cellar_3.if.q_eel_3.tell.0: Since Sunday the pilgrims kneel at the north well. Afterwards some come on here and pay to look at a crack.
dlg.q_gate_2.if.q_cellar_2.sell.0: The bats in the net come from the inn, I hear. The innkeeper says they are part of the tour.
dlg.q_gate_2.if.q_cellar_2.seal.0: Half of them are from the inn. When the mason walled up its cellar, they had nowhere to go but my gate.
dlg.q_ysa.offer.0: Ysa brings my salves in from the wood every new moon. Thirty years, never late. She is two moons late.
dlg.q_ysa.offer.1: I went out to her farm myself. Door open, nobody home. Find her. Try the glade first; she picks there.
dlg.q_ysa.more.0: Yes, wolves. I thought of wolves. I also thought of my orders. A man can think two things at once.
dlg.q_ysa.more.1: The cook at the inn burned both hands at midsummer. People are waiting on that salve. So am I.
dlg.q_ysa.wait.0: Any sign? People ask me for salve. I tell them soon. Soon is wearing thin.
dlg.q_ysa.found.0: Pell sent you? I came up after lunch. He can wait for his jars like everyone else.
dlg.q_ysa.reply.found: It's been two months out there.
dlg.q_ysa.found.1: Has it. ...Look at that bee. It's been on that flower since I sat down.
dlg.q_ysa.found.2: I'll walk home. Go and tell Pell his jars are coming. He'll want to count them.
dlg.q_ysa.done.1: So she's home. She'll bring the jars. She will, won't she? Here. For your boots.
dlg.q_book.offer.0: Eleven jars gone off my shelf, and Marra's book off my table. Jars, anyone takes. A book, you take if you read.
dlg.q_book.offer.1: Pell reads. He reads my bills to me, wrong. Find the book at his place and take it to Brannoc the smith. It was his gran's.
dlg.q_book.more.0: Marra walked out for salve every month, thirty years. Wrote in that book at my table. Never once burned herself.
dlg.q_book.more.1: I can't read a word of it. Kept it three winters. If a thief can reach it, it can go to her boy.
dlg.q_book.wait.0: Still looking? Pell keeps everything that matters behind his counter. Including himself.
dlg.q_book.done.0: Gran's hand. Hinges for the town gate. I held those while she swore at them.
dlg.q_book.done.1: Last page. 'Hammer's under Ysa's step.' ...That's all it says.
dlg.q_book.done.2: Don't go far. I've a letter to write, and I write slow.
dlg.q_book.after.pell.0: Somebody's been behind my counter. Nothing's missing. Nothing I can mention.
dlg.q_book.after.pell.1: I've bought a lock. Thieves everywhere these days. I'd know.
dlg.q_letter.offer.0: Kell. My cousin, the smith down the road. He thinks Gran's hammer should be his. He hears this from me first.
dlg.q_letter.offer.1: In writing, so he can't say he wasn't told. Take it to him. Then come back, and we'll talk about a step.
dlg.q_letter.more.0: Thirty years at her anvil. He sat with her the last month. Talked her ear off.
dlg.q_letter.more.1: Three winters on a borrowed hammer. Hers never cooled. Hang it on a nail at night, it's warm by morning.
dlg.q_letter.wait.0: He'll shout. Let him. Shouting's not an answer.
dlg.q_letter.done.0: From BRANNOC? Give it here. ...'The hammer goes with the forge.' Does it. DOES it.
dlg.q_letter.done.1: I sat with her every night the last month. He came twice. Here. For your walk, not his letter. Your WALK.
dlg.ysa.lifted.0: Under my step? Marra mended that step every spring. It never once needed mending.
dlg.ysa.lifted.1: Wolves have gone round this house three winters. I put it down to luck. Luck's cheaper than walls.
dlg.ysa.lifted.2: Take it, if her boys want it. She hated a thing that just sat there.
dlg.ysa.gone.0: The wolves found my step last night. Three winters they couldn't find it.
dlg.ysa.gone.1: I sleep with the poker now. Don't say sorry. Say something useful, or nothing.
dlg.q_hammer_b.offer.0: He got it? Good. Now he can't say he wasn't told.
dlg.q_hammer_b.offer.1: Ysa's step. The herb-woman, out in the wood. Bring the hammer here.
dlg.q_hammer_b.more.0: Thirty years she walked out there. For burns, she said. I never saw her burn.
dlg.q_hammer_b.more.1: Kell asked you something. Don't tell me what. I'd only have to believe it.
dlg.q_hammer_b.wait.0: Not yet? It's a step. It isn't going anywhere.
dlg.q_hammer_b.done.0: That's it. Still warm. Three winters under a step, and still warm.
dlg.q_hammer_b.done.1: I'll make you something with it. First thing it's hit in three winters. Then it hangs over the fire.
dlg.q_hammer_b.closed.0: Kell's got it. Course he has. You were always going to.
dlg.q_hammer_b.closed.1: He'll hang it where people can see it. That's all he ever wanted from her.
dlg.q_hammer_b.after.0: Hear that? That's her ring. Thirty years I woke to it.
dlg.q_hammer_b.after.1: Don't lean on the anvil. It's working again.
dlg.q_hammer_k.offer.0: He knows where it is, doesn't he. And so do YOU. It's all over your face.
dlg.q_hammer_k.offer.1: Get there before him and bring Gran's hammer HERE. By his letter that's stealing. Fine. FINE. Steal it.
dlg.q_hammer_k.more.0: She walked to that wood every month! Her hands were leather! What was she salving? ...Never mind. NEVER mind.
dlg.q_hammer_k.more.1: I'll pay more than he would. He's tight. She told him so to his face; it was the only way to tell him anything.
dlg.q_hammer_k.wait.0: Got it? Don't walk past his forge with it. He can hear iron think.
dlg.q_hammer_k.done.0: There she is. Feel that! Three winters, and warm as a loaf.
dlg.q_hammer_k.done.1: Your pay. More than his. If he asks, you never met me. Nobody believes that, but say it.
dlg.q_hammer_k.closed.0: You took it to HIM. Course you did. Everyone does what Brannoc says. Even she did, some days.
dlg.q_hammer_k.closed.1: Fine. FINE. A borrowed hammer. Terrible thing. Mine, though.
dlg.q_hammer_k.after.0: Hear that ring? Folk come from the square to listen. Nobody tell Brannoc.
dlg.q_hammer_k.after.1: It hangs over the door now. People touch it for luck. I let them.
dlg.q_herbs.offer.0: Two months gone, and my shelf's bare. Winter won't wait for me to catch up.
dlg.q_herbs.offer.1: Slowleaf grows in the glade. Pick me {count}, and pick standing up.
dlg.q_herbs.more.0: It keeps all winter, picked up there. Don't ask me why. Ask the bees.
dlg.q_herbs.wait.0: Don't sit down up there. I did.
dlg.q_herbs.done.0: Good pick. You left the roots. Somebody raised you, then.
dlg.q_herbs.done.1: Here. It's not much. There'll be a jar for you come winter, if you're anywhere I can find.
dlg.q_herbs.after.0: Salve's setting. Pell can buy it like everyone else. At my price.
dlg.q_herbs.after.1: Kettle's on. Don't stay long. You'll forget to get up.
